translationRepairs: Hart, courtesy name Lubin, was from Belfast in Ireland.
Hart, courtesy name Lubin, was from Belfast in Britain.
s0131 reads 英國倍爾發司人; the source places Belfast in Britain (英國) and never names Ireland. Replacing Ireland with Britain restores the Chinese polity label without other change.
In 1889, when Tibetan troops raided Bhutan and British forces intervened, Hart sent his brother Commissioner Hart to Tibet to negotiate the boundary with the resident commissioner.
In 1889, when Tibetan troops raided Sikkim and British forces intervened, Hart sent his brother Commissioner Hart to Tibet to negotiate the boundary with the resident commissioner.
s0147 has 藏兵寇哲孟雄; 哲孟雄 is Sikkim, not Bhutan (不丹). The proposed idiomatic corrects that place-name error and otherwise preserves the sentence.

In the fifteenth year Tibetan troops raided Bhutan; British troops took advantage to intrude; Hart sent his younger brother, Customs Commissioner Hart junior, posthaste to confer with the resident commissioner in Tibet on boundary matters.

In the fifteenth year Tibetan troops raided Sikkim; British troops took advantage to intrude; Hart sent his younger brother, Customs Commissioner Hart junior, posthaste to confer with the resident commissioner in Tibet on boundary matters.
The same 哲孟雄 in s0147 must be Sikkim in the literal; Bhutan invents the wrong polity. The proposed replacement fixes only that toponym.
After the 1911 revolution he died in office and received generous posthumous honors.
After the 1911 revolution he died of illness and received generous posthumous honors.
s0159 is 辛亥後，病卒，賜優恤; 病卒 means he died of illness. “Died in office” invents a circumstance absent from the Chinese; the proposed wording restores 病卒 accurately.
He concluded joint postal regulations with France, Germany, and British India.
He concluded joint postal regulations with France, Germany, and British Natal.
s0174 names 英屬那達, distinct from 英屬印度 in s0172; 那達 is Natal. British India misreads that toponym, and British Natal matches the Chinese.
